pr_title: Keep M01/M02 local gates honest with usecase boundary
summary: F7 security review for PR #8: reviewed gate boundary changes and reviewer/fix-loop runtime surfaces; 3 actionable findings, highest severity BLOCKER.

findings.issue: The dispatcher defaults to External runtime mode; the workflow does not pass --runtime-mode; and tests lock the empty-panel behavior as APPROVE with subagent_runtime_pending=true plus a pr-review-approved event. That is a fail-open review signal unless every downstream consumer independently rejects the pending flag.
findings.remediation: Change missing/incomplete panels to CHANGES_REQUESTED or REJECT at the dispatcher boundary, and make the workflow pass an explicit runtime mode only when a complete panel is produced.

findings.issue: The architecture-boundary gate still allows transitional application/runtime roles and broad runtime dependencies. For security-sensitive code, legacy role aliases can keep adapter/secret/runtime concerns outside the intended usecase/app boundary without a mechanical sunset.
findings.remediation: Add a dated ratchet fixture that fails new catalog records using application/runtime/test aliases and remove the aliases once the named migration follow-ups land.

findings.issue: The fix-loop dispatcher treats runtime invocation failure as non-fatal and continues dispatching a bundle with subagent_runtime_pending=true. This preserves recovery, but it also emits a next-step path that can be mistaken for an active fix-loop unless admission consistently refuses the pending flag.
findings.remediation: Make the dispatcher exit non-zero for runtime invocation failure in automated CI, or emit only a blocked/escalation artifact until a real runtime response exists.
